vulnerability_type: Missing authentication for a critical function, gated on a hardcoded public constant
summary: A QR code containing factory://factory-aae949f6969-lorem-ipsum-data forces any badge into the factory standalone test mode, because the only check is string equality against a constant published in this open source repository.
explanation: FACTORY_STANDALONE_STRING at ux.rs:29 is a compile-time constant with a randomised-looking substring, used as though it were a shared secret. The QR handler reaches the comparison on the path taken when base45 decoding fails, splits the input on "://" and dispatches by scheme; the factory arm assigns VaultMode::StandAloneTest on equality with no further gate, no button confirmation and no check that the module is detached from the badge carrier.
malicious_actor: proximate stranger with no credentials, able to display a QR code to the victim badge
parameter: QR code payload, the factory:// scheme string (optical scan)
trigger_flow: attacker QR code -> VaultOp::HandleQr -> base45 decode fails -> split_once("://") -> factory arm -> data == FACTORY_STANDALONE_STRING -> VaultMode::StandAloneTest
malicious_input_example: a QR code encoding the exact string factory://factory-aae949f6969-lorem-ipsum-data
